title: Πάτηρ καὶ θυγατέρες
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 299. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔχων τις δύο θυγατέρας, τὴν μὲν κηπουρῷ ἐξέδωκε πρὸς γάμον, τὴν δὲ ἑτέραν κεραμεῖ.
sentences.tr: Echōn tis dyo thygateras, tēn men kēpourōi exedōke pros gamon, tēn de heteran keramei.
sentences.l: A certain man, having two daughters, gave the one to a gardener in marriage, and the other to a potter.
sentences.n: ἐκδίδωμι, 'give out', is the regular word for a father's bestowing a daughter in marriage; the daughter is given away from the house. τὴν μέν … τὴν δέ divides the pair, and the whole fable turns on the division. A note on the number: Chambry's editio minor prints no fable numbered 298 — the numeral 299 stands over this fable and over the one before it alike, a compositor's slip. This edition publishes the first of the pair as 298 and this one as 299; the Greek itself is untouched.

sentences.t: Χρόνου δὲ προελθόντος, ἧκεν ὡς τὴν τοῦ κηπουροῦ καὶ ταύτην ἠρώτα πῶς ἔχοι καὶ ἐν τίνι αὐτοῖς εἴη τὰ πράγματα.
sentences.tr: Chronou de proelthontos, hēken hōs tēn tou kēpourou kai tautēn ērōta pōs echoi kai en tini autois eiē ta pragmata.
sentences.l: And time having gone forward, he came to the one who was the gardener's, and asked her how she was, and in what case their affairs stood for them.
sentences.i: As time went on he came to the gardener's wife, and asked her how she was, and how matters stood with them.
sentences.n: Genitive absolute for the passage of time. τὴν τοῦ κηπουροῦ leaves the noun unexpressed — 'the gardener's woman', i.e. his wife; Greek does this freely with the article and a genitive. ὡς with the accusative of a person is 'to the house of'. ἔχω with an adverb is the ordinary way of saying how a person is faring, and ἔχοι and εἴη are optatives of the indirect question in secondary sequence.

sentences.t: Τῆς δὲ εἰπούσης πάντα μὲν αὐτοῖς παρεῖναι, ἓν δὲ τοῦτο εὔχεσθαι τοῖς θεοῖς, ὅπως χειμὼν γένηται καὶ ὄμβρος, ἵνα τὰ λάχανα ἀρδευθῇ, μετ’ οὐ πολὺ παρεγένετο πρὸς τὴν τοῦ κεραμέως καὶ αὐτῆς ἐπυνθάνετο πῶς ἔχοι.
sentences.tr: Tēs de eipousēs panta men autois pareinai, hen de touto euchesthai tois theois, hopōs cheimōn genētai kai ombros, hina ta lachana ardeuthēi, met’ ou poly paregeneto pros tēn tou kerameōs kai autēs epynthaneto pōs echoi.
sentences.l: And when she said that everything was at hand for them, but that they prayed to the gods for this one thing, that foul weather might come and rain, so that the greens might be watered, not long after he arrived at the one who was the potter's and inquired of her how she was.
sentences.i: And she said that they had everything they needed, and prayed the gods for one thing only, that foul weather and rain should come to water the greens; and not long after he came to the potter's wife and asked her how she was.
sentences.n: χειμών is winter and equally the storm that winter brings; here it is the wet weather a gardener wants, and it must keep that sense when the father sets χειμῶνα against εὐδία in his closing question. ὅπως with the subjunctive gives the content of the prayer, ἵνα with the subjunctive its purpose. The whole reply is carried in infinitives, the regular form of reported speech after a verb of saying.

sentences.t: Τῆς δὲ τὰ μὲν ἄλλα μὴ ἐνδεῖσθαι εἰπούσης, τοῦτο δὲ μόνον εὔχεσθαι, ὅπως αἰθρία τε λαμπρὰ ἐπιμείνῃ καὶ λαμπρὸς ἥλιος, ἵνα ξηρανθῇ ὁ κέραμος, εἶπε πρὸς αὐτήν· « Ἐὰν σὺ μὲν εὐδίαν ἐπιζητῇς, ἡ δὲ ἀδελφή σου χειμῶνα, ποτέρᾳ ὑμῶν συνεύξομαι ; »
sentences.tr: Tēs de ta men alla mē endeisthai eipousēs, touto de monon euchesthai, hopōs aithria te lampra epimeinēi kai lampros hēlios, hina xēranthēi ho keramos, eipe pros autēn· « Ean sy men eudian epizētēis, hē de adelphē sou cheimōna, poterāi hymōn syneuxomai ; »
sentences.l: And when she said that in all else they were in no want, but that they prayed for this alone, that a bright clear sky might hold and a bright sun, so that the clay might be dried, he said to her: « If you seek fair weather and your sister foul, with which of the two of you shall I join my prayer? »
sentences.i: And she said that they wanted for nothing else, and prayed only that clear sky and bright sun should hold, so that the clay might dry; whereupon he said to her: « If you are asking for fair weather and your sister for foul, which of the two of you am I to pray with? »
sentences.n: ἐνδέομαι, 'be in want of', with τὰ ἄλλα as accusative of respect: short of nothing in other regards. ὁ κέραμος is the potter's ware, the clay that must dry before firing. συνεύχομαι takes the dative of the one whose prayer you join, and ποτέρᾳ is the dative of πότερος, the word used when the choice lies between two. The Greek question mark is a semicolon, and Chambry's house style sets a space before it.

sentences.t: Οὕτως οἱ ἐν ταὐτῷ τοῖς ἀνομοίοις πράγμασιν ἐπιχειροῦντες εἰκότως περὶ τὰ ἑκάτερα πταίουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtōs hoi en tautōi tois anomoiois pragmasin epicheirountes eikotōs peri ta hekatera ptaiousin.
sentences.l: So those who at one and the same time set their hand to unlike undertakings, with good reason come to grief in each of the two.
sentences.n: ἐν ταὐτῷ is a crasis of ἐν τῷ αὐτῷ, 'in the same', of time as of place: at once. ἑκάτερα is 'each of the two' — not both taken together but each side of the pair in turn, which is exactly the father's difficulty. πταίω is to stumble, and so to come off badly.
